hints: Focus on the functional groups present, especially whether each molecule has H attached directly to O or N.
Only $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$ has an $\text{O-H}$ group, so only it can donate a hydrogen bond to another molecule of itself.
Recall the strength order where hydrogen bonding is much stronger than permanent dipole-dipole forces, so the hydrogen-bonded liquid will need the most energy to boil.
walkthrough:
**Look at what each molecule can do**

All three molecules have a similar $M_r$ around 44 to 46, so size is not the deciding factor. What matters is the type of intermolecular force each can form with itself.

Structures to compare:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} \text{ , } \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} \text{ , } \text{CH}_3\text{OCH}_3$$

**Check for hydrogen bonding**

For hydrogen bonding between identical molecules you need H attached directly to N, O or F. Only ethanol has this, in its $\text{-O-H}$ group.

$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{O-H} \cdots \text{O(H)C}_2\text{H}_5$$

**Compare with the other two compounds**

Ethanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$) is polar because of $\text{C=O}$, and methoxymethane ($\text{CH}_3\text{OCH}_3$) is polar because of $\text{C-O}$, so their strongest forces are permanent dipole-dipole forces. They have no $\text{O-H}$ hydrogen, so they cannot hydrogen bond to themselves.

Strength order:
$$\text{hydrogen bonds > permanent dipole-dipole forces}$$

**Pick the highest boiling point**

Stronger attractions need more thermal energy to break when boiling. So ethanol, with intermolecular hydrogen bonds, has the highest boiling point.

options.A: Methoxymethane has no O-H bond, so it cannot form hydrogen bonds with itself. Its main force is permanent dipole-dipole plus induced dipole-dipole forces, and it actually has the lowest boiling point of the three.
options.B: The interaction is right for ethanol but the compound is wrong. Ethanal has a polar C=O bond and can accept hydrogen bonds from water, but with no H on O it cannot donate hydrogen bonds to another ethanal molecule.
options.C: Ethanol is correct. Its -OH group allows strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds (O-H...O) between ethanol molecules. These are much stronger than the permanent dipole-dipole forces in the other two, so ethanol needs the most energy to separate and has the highest boiling point.
options.D: The interaction described for ethanal is correct, permanent dipole-dipole forces from the polar C=O group, but ethanal does not have the highest boiling point. This trap rewards students who remember ethanal is polar but forget that hydrogen bonding is stronger.
